- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/item-lock.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e540e7ffb9b9a9cfc9897722c2e04941e9924a8e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `950976fc84ad7b1254c5a9b737ea919d2cb826a1` — the merge of head `010639549d199247daa802e778966a86f29f6c62` into base `e540e7ffb9b9a9cfc9897722c2e04941e9924a8e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh

git fetch origin 950976fc84ad7b1254c5a9b737ea919d2cb826a1 && git checkout 950976fc84ad7b1254c5a9b737ea919d2cb826a1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e540e7ffb9b9a9cfc9897722c2e04941e9924a8e 010639549d199247daa802e778966a86f29f6c62 && git checkout -B drift-repro e540e7ffb9b9a9cfc9897722c2e04941e9924a8e && git merge --no-ff 010639549d199247daa802e778966a86f29f6c62

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e540e7ffb9b9a9cfc9897722c2e04941e9924a8e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a

> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than

> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e540e7ffb9b9a9cfc9897722c2e04941e9924a8e` → pass the list as

Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing below re-derives one.

### ① Derived judgments

**The direction: right.** `authoredLockFamily` is called once, inside the author arm (`request.source === undefined && request.writeFace !== 'package-duplicate'`), on the line after `protectionBlockRefusal`; the `else` arm (`withoutProtectionBlock`) is byte-identical, so `source` and `package-duplicate` writes keep stamping (pinned for both faces, and the stamp survives author saves on both author faces). Three outcomes, as triage binds: no `_lock*` key, and `withLockFamily(body, stored)` writes the row's stored family back onto the body (a carry-forward, not a removal; the fail-open the dev measured on base, a stamped `no-delete` lost to the next author save, is closed and pinned); an echo, accepted, and the body still gets the stored family, so the row keeps its own; anything else, `authoredLockFamilyRefusal`, nothing written. No silent strip: the only key removal is of a family equal to the served one on a row that stores none (the packaged first overlay), which is "ignored", not "stripped". No stored lock is unbound: every path through the method writes `stored` onto the body or throws. `stripUnmanagedImportLock` and `importUnmanagedPackage` are not in the diff. Position against the gates: the L3 gate `assertLockAllowsWrite` runs above the arm, so `full` and `no-overlay` still answer `403 ITEM_LOCKED` before any family judgement (pinned); the per-type parse and the destructive diff run below it.

**The echo test: the served set, no wider and no narrower.** Traced on the head. The active item read (`getMetaItem`) serves its body through `mergeArtifactProtection(..., itemLock)`, which is `withItemLockFamily(item, resolveItemLock({ artifact: artifactLockLayerAt(address), overlay: overlayLockLayerAt(address, { otherSpelling: true }) }))`; the layered read's `effective` and the list (`readFlattenedMetaItems`) serve the same family. That is echo source 1, computed in the arm with the same two layer readers and `otherSpelling: true`. The draft read (`state: 'draft'`) returns the draft row's body verbatim (it returns before the overlay-lock read), the `previewDrafts` arm returns the draft row verbatim (`convertStoredItem` of the row), and the layered `overlay` layer is the row as stored: echo source 2, the row the save writes, read through `repo.headAt(ref, { state, packageId: args.packageId ?? null, member })`, the same write-address resolution `storedHeadAt` uses one call later for the version lock, with the first-draft fallback to the active row at `target.packageId` (the inherited binding); `rowToItem` hands the raw stored body, so the compare is byte-faithful. The layered `code` layer is the one served document outside the set (the dev's declared boundary, flag 6). A family copied from another item passes only when it is equal in value to one of this item's two families, in which case it is indistinguishable from an echo and is ignored (the row keeps its own); the clone pin covers the other case (a stamped family on an unlocked clone target: refused, no row). The packaged first overlay: the pin has the row storing none and `getMetaItem` still answering `lock: 'no-delete', deletable: false` through the artifact layer, so the package's lock keeps binding. One asymmetry, not a defect: `previewDrafts` serves the draft row while a publish-mode save compares against the active row, so a verbatim echo of a legacy draft whose family differs from the active row's is refused on a publish-mode save; that save would change the active row's lock, refusal is the rule, the message carries the remedy, and the population is rows written before this change.

**The early return: right, and it never stores.** For each sent key whose declared schema (`overlaySchemaDeclaredKey`, the walker `protectionBlockRefusal` uses) refuses the value, the body is returned unchanged. The per-type parse at the bottom of `saveMetaItem` (`resolveOverlaySchema(request.type, request.item).safeParse`) runs for every face in both modes with no `force` or draft exemption, and `_lock*` is declared wherever `MetadataProtectionFields` is spread, so the same value fails there and the save throws `422 INVALID_METADATA` before the put (four values pinned, no metadata write). A malformed-but-schema-passing value cannot exist: the arm's check and the parse apply the same declared schema to the same value. A type with no schema (`external_catalog`) skips the early return and is judged (pinned). `LOCK_FAMILY_KEYS`, derived from `MetadataProtectionFields`, is exactly the four keys `item-lock.ts` hard-codes (`_lock`, `_lockReason`, `_lockSource`, `_lockDocsUrl`); the PR body's "no third hand-kept list" is off by one (item-lock keeps the second), prose only.

**The faces: each judged right; none is server-stated in fact.** `meta-envelope` (the REST `PUT`, built field by field) and `meta-dispatch`: the author's body, judged, both pinned across every case. No face: the flow save (`automation.ts` stores "the definition as the caller's door built it"), judged, right; the flow and permission-set clones delete every key of `MetadataProtectionFields` before saving, so they send no family; the permission-set data door saves `getMetaItemLayered().overlay` (the stored row verbatim) into that row's own package (`storedRowPackageArg`), echo source 2; the permission-set and position backfills and the position write-through build their bodies from data rows (`permissionSetBodyFromRow`, `positionBodyFromRow`), no family; the package publish's app flip re-saves the list's served body with `packageId: id`, echo source 1. `external-import`: the body is server-built, and no file under `packages/services/service-datasource/src` mentions `_lock`; carry-forward only. `package-unmanaged-import`: `stripUnmanagedImportLock` removes all four keys when every present one parses, and hands a body with a non-parsing one on untouched, where the arm's early return leaves it to the parse's 422, as before; the import writes with `mode: 'publish'` into names no row holds, so a stripped body carries nothing forward. No door the dispatch names carries a server-stamped lock through the author arm, so nothing legitimate is refused or dropped.

**The envelope: right.** `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, `issues[]` one entry per sent key with `code: 'custom'` (the `MetadataIssueEntry` shape), the family and position of `protectionBlockRefusal`; `resolveThrownHttpError` carries `issues` for any status (established in 6135514431). The message prescribes first ("Remove ... and send it again. Nothing was written."), names the effect (set, change, remove), the ADR-0010 clause and the one door (a code package's `protection`, Phase 4.3), and stays well under the 500-character REST bound for ordinary names. Nit, prose only: a lone prose key on an unlocked item (`_lockReason` alone) is described as "would set a lock on it"; it sets no lock, and the refusal is still right.

**The edited tests: faithful re-pins.** `protocol.package-publish-audit-rows.test.ts`: the five fixtures lock the ACTIVE row after staging drafts; they now do it with `source: 'migrate-stored', force: true`, the call shape `migrateStoredMetadata` itself makes on the head, and every assertion (batch abort, rollback, denied rows) is untouched; `auditedBefore` is snapshotted after the fixture, so the fixture's own audit rows never enter a count. `protocol-derived-provenance-doors.test.ts`: the old pin stored an author-written family verbatim; the new pair keeps the intent it was written for (the three derived keys go and the family is not stripped: a stamped family survives an author echo of the derived keys) and adds the refusal with nothing written. No weakening.

**`item-lock.ts`: prose only.** The diff replaces two docblock lines with six; `ITEM_LOCK_LAYERS`, `resolveItemLock`, `firstBindingLayer`, `resolveOverlayLockLayer`, `resolveArtifactLockLayer` and `withItemLockFamily` are byte-identical, and the amended sentence states 6135754247's reading.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`: right. The act narrows a published accept set (a body the door stored now answers 400), so it is breaking and not the "changes no public surface stays `patch`" case; `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` states that in the launch window a breaking change ships `minor`, the `**BREAKING**` banner and the ADR-0087 disposition carry the breaking-ness, and the level axis stands down on a `no` declaration. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the arm `clause2-line.mjs` defines as "NOT a widening, but breaking", which is this diff. No `@objectstack/spec` entry: that package's text is not in the diff.

`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right. The gate refuses the category only where the changeset's body prescribes a rewrite of a consumer's code or metadata; this remedy is a request value at one runtime door, the `FROM / TO / Remedy` shape 6135514431 accepted for `23096-save-door-protection` and five stock entries. A ledger entry would be wrong, not merely unneeded: no stored row is rewritten, and an ADR-0087 conversion replays over package sources, where `_lock*` is the loader's legitimate stamp. Check Changeset and the lint family that runs the gate are green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **BLOCKING: a same-release contract contradiction this PR's changeset must supersede, the class 6135514431 flag 1 named on the sibling.** `.changeset/23096-save-door-protection.md` sits in `origin/main`'s unreleased stock and states, under "Unchanged": "A body without `protection` saves as before." At this head a body without `protection` that carries an authored `_lock*` family answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` (this PR's own FROM and TO). Both bodies ship verbatim into one `CHANGELOG.md` release of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, so the release contradicts itself on one input. The PR body's claim that "No sentence of a pending `15213-*` or `23096-*` entry becomes false" is wrong on this sentence. Fix, one sentence in `.changeset/23119-save-door-lock-envelope.md`, in the house form the sibling itself uses: "This entry supersedes one sentence of the entry `23096-save-door-protection`, in this same release", stating that its "A body without `protection` saves as before" now holds for a body that also sends no `_lock*` key or echoes the served family, while a body whose family would set, change or remove the lock is refused as this entry states. Nothing else moves. The `15213-*` entries stay true: the unmanaged install still strips a parseable family, and a non-parsing one still meets the parse's 422.
2. Base `f931e765b7` instead of `0d43004100`: the merge-base against `origin/main` is `f931e765b7`, one spec/ui commit past the claim's tree; the touched surface is identical and the diff applies cleanly against today's `main`. Not blocking.
3. Hunks beyond the arm: five module-level helpers beside `protectionBlockRefusal`, one private method above `saveMetaItem`, one import; the arm gains one call. All in `protocol.ts`, all needed by the rule. Not blocking.
4. Existing test files edited: both relied on the author face storing a lock, the behaviour this card reverses; neither is one of #22962's files; the ledger json is gate-prescribed (three rows, none lost). Not blocking.
5. Measurement at the protocol door rather than a showcase boot: the REST `PUT`, `GET` and `DELETE` forward to the three methods measured, the arm sits in the protocol, and Build Core and Dogfood Regression Gate are green. Not blocking.
6. The two noted findings: rows and pending drafts that already store an author-written lock keep it, and publishing such a draft still promotes it: that is the triage's own line (this card unbinds nothing; a stuck item is the §3.8 card). A body copied from the layered `code` layer with `_lock: 'none'`: refused loudly with a one-step remedy; the layer is raw by another lane's ruling and is not a Studio round-trip source. Neither blocking. Same class, noted for the owning seat's list: `restoreVersion` and `rollbackMetaItem` reach `put` without the arm, so a historical body written before this change can bring its author-written family back; existing state, no new door.
7. Dev deviations, each answered: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR's line 2 against the claim's bare `no`: right, the arm is what `clause2-line.mjs` asks of a breaking non-widening (②); the verify-lock narrowing and the one re-run: process, no effect on the diff.
8. One Test Core shard (4/6) was still running at the poll above; the landing waits on it whatever this verdict says.

The seat re-read the blocking item before adopting it: `.changeset/23096-save-door-protection.md` on `origin/main` says under **Unchanged** "A body without `protection` saves as before." The verdict holds. The dev adds the supersession sentence in a patch round, and a delta record runs on the new head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `010639549d199247daa802e778966a86f29f6c62`
Local-runs: none

Delta record after the FAIL 6138876344 on `6bbc5475cc`. Inputs: card #23119 (body; comments 6135754247 triage, 6136862148 unlock, 6136889453 claim, 6138569909 and 6139133868 the dev reports for round 0 and patch round 1); PR #23167 (its seat-edited body, the 7-file list, the net diff against the merge-base `f931e765b7` with `origin/main` at `e540e7ffb9`, the delta `6bbc5475cc..010639549d`, its comments: the prior record and the docs-drift comment); the check-runs on the head; `.changeset/23096-save-door-protection.md` and the four `.changeset/15213-*.md` entries on `origin/main`. Read-only: git reads of the fetched ref `refs/review/pr-23167-r1` and REST reads; nothing built, run or re-run. The delta is re-judged in full; the rest of 6138876344 is confirmed on this head, not re-derived.

Check-runs on the head, polled 2026-10-13T05:51Z: 46 runs, 36 success, 8 skipped (opt-in or path-gated: Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, Dogfood Verify CLI, the Dogfood Regression shard matrix, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke, and the second Auto Label and Check PR Size runs that the body edit at 2026-10-13T05:47Z re-triggered), 2 still running: Test Core 3/6 and 4/6. Green includes Check Changeset twice (the run the push started and the run the body edit started), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test Core 1/6, 2/6, 5/6 and 6/6, every Lint family (ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, the CI/release/engine gates, the repo and tooling gates, the docs and code guards, the three scoped lints), every Type Check family (source gates, debt ledger, consumer gates, workspace, and TypeScript Type Check), Check Documentation Links, and the claim, single-writer and part-of guards. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing below re-derives one.

### ① Derived judgments

**The delta is what the dev reports, and nothing else.** `git diff 6bbc5475cc..010639549d`: three files, +5/-2. `.changeset/23119-save-door-lock-envelope.md`: one paragraph and its blank line, inserted between the envelope paragraph and FROM. `protocol.ts`: one line in `authoredLockFamilyRefusal`, where the `servedLock === 'none'` branch of the `effect` ternary now reads `(sentLock === 'none' ? 'add lock keys to it' : 'set a lock on it')`. `protocol.save-door-lock-family.test.ts`: the add pin's expected effect becomes `family._lock && family._lock !== 'none' ? 'set a lock on it' : 'add lock keys to it'`, plus one comment line. No other hunk: `item-lock.ts`, the two re-pinned test files, the ledger json and every other line of `protocol.ts` are byte-identical to `6bbc5475cc`, so every ① judgment of 6138876344 (the arm's position after `protectionBlockRefusal` inside the author arm with the `else` arm untouched, the echo set of exactly two families, the early return to the parse's 422, the faces, the envelope, the faithful re-pins, `item-lock.ts` prose only) holds on this head unchanged.

**The supersession paragraph: true at this head, in the house form, naming the sentence exactly.** Form: it is the skeleton `23096-save-door-protection` itself uses to supersede `15213-unmanaged-lock-strip`, clause for clause (the bold lead "This entry supersedes one sentence of the entry …, in this same release.", then "That entry says …", "What holds now: …", "Where the two entries disagree, this one is current."), at the same place in the entry (after the explanatory paragraph, before FROM). Quotation: "A body without `protection` saves as before" is the first sentence of the sibling's Unchanged bullet, character for character, backticks included, and "under its unchanged behaviour" names that bullet. Truth against the code: a body with no `_lock*` key passes the arm through `withLockFamily(body, stored)`, so it is accepted as before; a family equal to the stored row's (`repo.headAt` at the save's state, package and member, the active row for a first draft) or to the resolved served family (`resolveItemLock` over `artifactLockLayerAt` and `overlayLockLayerAt` with `otherSpelling: true`) passes; any other family throws `authoredLockFamilyRefusal`, `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, before `put`. "Sends back exactly the `_lock*` family a read of that item serves" covers both echo sources, since the draft read and the layered `overlay` layer serve the stored row and the item read, the layered `effective` and the list serve the resolved family. Two readings the paragraph leaves to the entry, neither a falsity: "saves as before" is the sibling's sense, accepted rather than refused at this door (the row now keeps a stamped family that the old door dropped, and this entry's FROM and TO state both halves); and the second clause names the set, change and remove class, while a non-binding family on an unlocked item (a lone prose key, `_lock: 'none'`) is refused too, under the first clause's "only when" and the entry's "Anything else is refused". A family with a value the declaration refuses meets the parse's 422 before and after, which the entry's Unchanged bullet states and the paragraph's "as this entry states" points at.

**No other sibling sentence turns false, unsuperseded.** Read every sentence of `23096-save-door-protection` and of the four pending `15213-*` entries on `origin/main` (`unmanaged-lock-strip`, `install-modes`, `unmanaged-import-verb`, `readonly-package-remedy`). Three of the `15213-*` entries moved between the merge-base and `e540e7ffb9` (#23126 landing: their stale supersession paragraphs and the "no door calls it yet" sentence were rewritten in place); the texts judged here are the current ones, and `23096-save-door-protection` is unchanged. 23096: "A packaged item's lock still binds … `403 ITEM_LOCKED` … before this refusal is asked" holds, since `assertLockAllowsWrite` runs above the arm (pinned: `full`, stamped, answers `ITEM_LOCKED` to a body with and without `_lock: 'none'`); "A row stored before this change keeps its bytes" holds, since no row is rewritten; its own supersession of 15213 holds, since `protectionBlockRefusal` runs before `authoredLockFamily` (a block beside a refused `_lock*` still meets the 400) and a refused `_lock*` value with no block still meets the 422 through the arm's early return (pinned, four values, no write). 15213-unmanaged-lock-strip: "writes every item without `_lock`, `_lockReason`, `_lockSource` and `_lockDocsUrl`" holds (`stripUnmanagedImportLock` and `importUnmanagedPackage` are not in the diff); "Refusals are unchanged … `422 INVALID_METADATA`" holds for its `_lock*` half (a value the declarations refuse is handed on, and the arm returns the body untouched to the parse), and the import writes a stripped body into names no row holds, so it never meets the new 400; "A managed install is unchanged" holds (the loader's stamp is not a save through the arm). 15213-unmanaged-import-verb's "the next save edits it" holds: the copy stores no family, and an author save with no family, or with an echo, passes. `install-modes` and `readonly-package-remedy` state nothing this door touches.

**The new wording: true for every input that reaches it; the envelope is unchanged.** `authoredLockFamilyRefusal` is reached only with a non-empty `sent` unequal to both the stored and the served family. `servedLock` is `served._lock ?? 'none'`, and `withItemLockFamily` writes no `_lock` key for a non-binding answer, so `servedLock === 'none'` is exactly "the item serves no lock". There: `sent._lock` absent (a lone prose key) or `'none'` reads "add lock keys to it", which is what accepting the body would do and no more; `'full'`, `'no-overlay'` or `'no-delete'` reads "set a lock on it". On a type with no schema (`external_catalog`) `sent._lock` may be any value: one that is neither absent nor `'none'` reads "set a lock on it" (the right refusal, the verb approximate), and `null` reads "add lock keys to it". The binding branches are untouched: a served lock met by `'none'` or by a body with no `_lock` reads "remove its lock" (accepting it would remove it), anything else "change its lock" (the partial echo that drops the prose included, pinned). Only the `effect` string moves: `code`, `status`, `issues[]` (one `custom` entry per sent key, the key as `path`), the prescription-first message, the ADR-0010 clause and the one door are the same bytes.
